newsitem.title: UK: AB Foods extends gains on acquisition hopes.
newsitem.headline: AB Foods extends gains on acquisition hopes.

text.p: Shares in Associated British Foods Plc extended their earlier gains in early afternoon trade on Tuesday, amid continued talk of an acquisition following last week's sale of its Irish supermarkets to Tesco Plc.
Dealers and analysts said AB Foods chairman Garry Weston was expected to strike an attractive deal, but said the stock may need some concrete news before it adds to recent sharp gains.
AB Foods shares were up 25-1/2p at 558-1/2 by 1450 GMT after earlier touching a record 560 -- some 16 percent above its level at the end of 1996.
"AB Foods has been doing well since the Tesco deal," said analyst John Campbell at Paribas Capital Markets.

"The cash pile is getting very big and with interest rates at a modest level they are just not going to get the yield. It makes sense to make an acquisition and the food sector is ripe for consolidation."

"Weston is a canny character and he is not going to overpay," Campbell said. "But the stock has probably been taken to a level where it can't go too much higher without real news, people want to see the shape of any deal that is done."
The Paribas analyst said high yields and low price-earnings ratios elsewhere in the food manufacturing sector could lure investors in the second quarter.
"Having been in the doldrums, the sector could start to show some momentum in the next few months," Campbell said.
